discussion_comments.comment_body:
`check_schema` uses unwrapped schema: `_M.schema` is wrapped via `batch_processor_manager:wrap_schema(schema)`, but `check_schema` validates against the raw `schema` for non-metadata types. This means batch processor config fields (e.g., `batch_max_size`) will fail validation. Please change to:
   ```lua
   return core.schema.check(_M.schema, conf)
   ```

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Hand-copying the redis fields per policy is the root cause of the sentinel, and it's still leaking: neither the `redis` nor the `redis-cluster` branch forwards `redis_keepalive_timeout` / `redis_keepalive_pool`, even though both are accepted (with defaults) by the schema branches you're reusing — see `apisix/utils/redis-schema.lua:47-52` and `:80-85`.

So today a user who sets them gets them silently dropped: `redis` falls back to the hardcoded `or 10000` / `or 100` in `limit-count/util.lua:177-178`, and `redis-cluster` passes `nil` into `utils/rediscluster.lua:27-28`.

Rather than patching two more lines, drive the copy from the schema you already have in hand — same trick `limit-count/init.lua:274-278` uses for the `group` whitelist:

```lua
local extra = policy_to_additional_properties[plugin_conf.policy]
if extra then
    for k in pairs(extra.properties) do
        limit_conf[k] = plugin_conf[k]
    end
end
```

That drops all three branches (46 lines) and makes future schema additions impossible to miss.

This is the lint failure (`line 128: getting the Lua global "os"`, same on 132).

Use `core.env.get("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST")`. `discovery/kubernetes/core.lua:74` already switched for this reason — `os.getenv` hits a lua-resty-core prefix-collision bug during worker init (#13055).

discussion_comments.comment_body:
The in-cluster default won't work. Workers only see env vars declared via an `env` directive, and `cli/ngx_tpl.lua` doesn't emit `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`/`_PORT`. So with the documented minimal config `{}` this is nil and you get `kubernetes_host is not set and KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST env var is missing`.

Either require users to declare both under `nginx_config.envs`, or drop the env fallback and require `kubernetes_host`. The doc table currently presents `$KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` as a working default.

No test covers this branch — every test passes an explicit `endpoint`.
